warning.text:
Swimming is currently prohibited in the Neckar in Stuttgart!

Open-water swimming should only be practiced by experienced swimmers.

items.title: Swimming guidelines
items.text: On federal waterways such as the Neckar, it is prohibited to swim in shipping lanes or within 100 metres of structures such as weirs, locks and bridges. Anyone who wants to swim in rivers safely should also follow a few rules.

items.title: Pollution
items.text: Following heavy rainfall, the river may temporarily become polluted with microorganisms. The water will remain contaminated for a further two to three days. For healthy people, the risk of serious illness is low. However, people with pre-existing medical conditions should be especially cautious.

items.title: Large Vessels
items.text: Ships up to 105 metres long travel on the Neckar. They cannot change course, which creates dangerous wake effects. Make sure you stay well away from the middle of the river and any shipping infrastructure.

items.title: Local Conditions
items.text: There are no designated swimming areas on the Neckar River. Anyone wishing to swim there should familiarise themselves with the local conditions. Dangerous currents can form near bridges, structures and boats. Poor visibility makes it harder to spot hazards beneath the water's surface.
